errorCodes.meaning: The named account does not exist at this mediator.

DeliveryState.description: `queued`: stored and not yet handed to the recipient. `delivered`: handed to the recipient (pickup or live stream) but not yet deleted by it — the recipient has not acknowledged it.
DeliveryState.title: DeliveryState

Ext.description: Vendor-namespaced extension object per SPEC.md §4.5.1. Each immediate key MUST be a reverse-DNS namespace; structure under each namespace is opaque to the framework.
Ext.title: Ext

MessageMeta.description: Metadata of one stored message. Never carries the message body.

deliveredAt.description: When the message was first handed to the recipient. Present only when deliveryState is `delivered`.

expiresAt.description: When the mediator will expire the message if it is not deleted first.

from.description: The sender, where the mediator knows it. Absent for anonymous messages.

msgId.description: The mediator's identifier for the stored message; the handle messaging/message/get and messaging/message/delete accept.

receivedAt.description: When the mediator stored the message.

MessageMeta.title: MessageMeta

Queue.description: Which of an account's two queues. `receive` holds messages addressed to the account awaiting its pickup. `send` holds messages the account sent that are still held against it until their recipient deletes them — so a stalled recipient fills its senders' send queues.
Queue.title: Queue

Response.description: The success response to a messaging/message/list request. Carried in a Trust Task document whose type is https://trusttasks.org/spec/messaging/message/list/0.1#response.

nextCursor.description: Opaque continuation token. Present only when further items remain beyond this page; omitted on the final page.

Response.title: Messaging — List Messages — response payload

Vid.description: A Verifiable Identifier (SPEC §4.8). For a mediator-served account this is the account's controlling DID, carried verbatim and compared by exact string equality. For privacy — and because some mediators key accounts by a one-way hash and never hold the full DID — a stable hash of the DID (e.g. its SHA-256 digest) is an equally valid value here: producer and consumer simply agree on the same opaque identifier and compare by exact string equality. The field carries whichever form the issuing mediator uses.
Vid.title: Vid

WireProtocol.description: The protocol a message travelled in, as the mediator detected it from the wire form. `didcomm` is DIDComm v2 (JWE/JWS); `didcommV1` is a DIDComm v1 envelope; `tsp` is a Trust Spanning Protocol message; `other` is anything the mediator could not classify.
WireProtocol.title: WireProtocol

cursor.description: Opaque continuation token from a prior page's nextCursor. Echoed verbatim; treated as unstructured by the requester.

did.description: The account whose queue to list. Omitted = the requester's own account. A requester without administrative standing may name only itself.

limit.description: Maximum messages per page. The mediator chooses a default when omitted.

peer.description: Only messages exchanged with this counterparty.
